model_note: AFC.NZ is NOT a growth-DCF candidate. Revenue has collapsed 78% YoY to NZ$161,285, the FY2026 audit contains a going-concern material uncertainty paragraph, the company has never generated repeatable positive owner FCF post-2020, and it survives on non-binding, discretionary loans/debt forgiveness from its controlling shareholder (NZ Silveray Group, 'NZSG'), which is simultaneously its largest creditor and largest customer (99.7% of receivables). A standard perpetuity-growth DCF off historical or projected FCF would be fiction. This model instead values the equity as a probability-weighted mix of (a) insolvency/wind-up, (b) a persisting shell worth roughly tangible book value plus a modest scarcity premium, and (c) speculative reverse-takeover (RTO) option value. The NZX minimum tick of NZ$0.001 has not moved since 2017 (see MonthlyPrices) and is a market-structure price FLOOR, not a fundamentals-derived market-clearing price.

inputs.net_debt_note: Total debt NZ$169,364 less cash NZ$39,437 (of which NZ$37,345 is restricted as a bank guarantee, leaving effectively negligible free cash). Net debt is already embedded inside reported shareholders' equity (NZ$206,390) and is NOT subtracted a second time in the scenario valuations below.
inputs.sbc_source: Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column is 0 for every period FY2017-FY2026; confirmed no share-based payment expense has ever been disclosed by AFC. No SBC adjustment is required (owner FCF = reported FCF).
inputs.shares_growth_note: No SBC, no buybacks, no disclosed dilutive instruments outside the speculative RTO scenario (where dilution to NEW consideration shares is qualitative, not modelled as a share-count mechanic - see bull case methodology).
inputs.units: absolute dollars (not thousands or millions) except shares_outstanding, which is in millions per Metrics.csv convention
inputs.related_party_payable_note: Owed to NZ Silveray Group Ltd at 10.08%-13.70% interest, subject only to a non-binding letter of support not to call the debt. NZSG advanced a further NZ$100,000 in April 2026 and NZ$100,000 in May 2026 (post year-end) - escalating reliance disclosed.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Not applicable in the conventional sense - both revenue CAGR (-46.9% 3yr / -24.3% 5yr) and equity CAGR (-18.0% 3yr / -30.7% 5yr) are deeply NEGATIVE, i.e. the business is shrinking/eroding on every historical measure, not diverging on growth. EPS and FCF CAGRs are reported as null/not meaningful because the base and intervening values cross zero or are immaterial pennies (e.g. FCF was +NZ$18,709 in FY2023, an isolated working-capital blip, versus -NZ$631,437 in FY2026), which makes a compound growth rate statistically meaningless rather than informative.
historical_growth.notes: Reported FCF has been positive in exactly one year since FY2020 (FY2023: +NZ$18,709, immaterial and driven by working-capital timing, not repeatable earnings power). Every other year FY2020-FY2026 shows negative FCF, with FY2026 the worst on record at -NZ$631,437 despite revenue also collapsing (i.e. the cost base has not shrunk proportionately with revenue). There is no meaningful FCF history to extrapolate a growth DCF from. Stock-based compensation is nil throughout the disclosed history, so no SBC/dilution adjustment is needed - the entire valuation problem here is going-concern risk and revenue collapse, not share-based dilution.

base.narrative: Shell persists on life support. NZSG continues discretionary funding/debt forgiveness (as it has every year to date: NZ$500,000 forgiven + NZ$281,170 interest waived in FY2026 alone). Wine and cosmetics operations continue at a de minimis, sub-scale level (minority 51% economic interest to AFC in both). No RTO completes within the valuation horizon. Value = current tangible shareholders' equity (which already nets off all debt, including the related-party NZSG loan) plus a conservative listed-shell scarcity premium.
base.shell_scarcity_value_note: NZX shell listings (a company retaining its listing but with minimal underlying operations) have historically transacted or been informally valued in the rough NZ$0.5-1.5M range to RTO promoters seeking a listed vehicle without a full IPO process. The LOW end of that range is used for the base case given AFC's below-average shell quality: vacant CEO seat for the full FY2026 year, non-independent chair, non-majority-independent board, recent forced auditor turnover, a July 2026 director resignation, and admitted non-compliance with numerous NZX Corporate Governance Code recommendations - all of which reduce (but do not eliminate) the shell's attractiveness relative to a 'clean' dormant listing.
base.burn_note: FY2027-FY2031 operating cash burn projection (funded, base case, by continued NZSG loans/forgiveness - consistent with the pattern of every year since FY2020). Shown for disclosure/schema completeness. NOT subtracted a second time from the tangible-equity valuation above, because the funding mechanism (new related-party debt or forgiveness) is a wash against equity as long as shareholder support continues - which is the base case's core assumption. If that assumption fails, that is definitionally the bear case, not a modification of the base case.
base.discounting_note: No perpetuity cash-flow stream exists to discount (burn is a funding wash, not a return to equity). WACC of 33% is disclosed for schema completeness and is used only in the entry-price 15%-hurdle comparison context, not to discount a terminal FCF.

bull.narrative: Reverse takeover (with 'Fast Track Group', currently at non-binding MOU stage, or another counterparty) completes. Existing shareholders are diluted by newly issued RTO consideration shares but retain a minority economic interest in whatever combined entity emerges, PLUS the value of the clean listing itself is realized. This is explicitly speculative OPTION VALUE, not a cash-flow DCF output - there is no disclosed transaction structure, exchange ratio, or timeline beyond 'MOU stage' as of the FY2026 annual report.
bull.methodology_note: Values the shell (i.e., the claim current shareholders hold on the listed vehicle PRIOR to issuance of new RTO consideration shares) at the upper end of NZX shell-value precedent, reflecting a completed transaction bringing in a genuine operating business and full governance remediation. This approximates the current shareholders' aggregate retained economic exposure as a minority stake in a re-rated entity, without attempting to model a specific dilution ratio or the acquired business's own cash flows (neither is disclosed). No new FCF projections are modelled for a hypothetical acquired business.

bear.narrative: Going-concern risk crystallizes: NZSG's discretionary, non-binding support is withdrawn or fails to materialize as promised (management explicitly discloses this dependency and its discretionary nature). Working-capital deficit (NZ$1.3M) and negative FY2026-year-end equity trajectory (H1-2026 equity was already negative, -NZ$120,066, before a year-end debt-forgiveness injection restored it to +NZ$206,390) force insolvency/liquidation. In a forced wind-up, realizable asset value (minority 51% stakes in a 4.22ha vineyard and an under-utilized face-mask plant, both illiquid and hard to sell quickly at book) falls short of liabilities (including the NZ$1.17M related-party loan and other payables), particularly once liquidation costs and minority-interest carve-outs are applied. Ordinary equity holders are wiped out.
bear.burn_note: FY2027 burn accelerates as support is withdrawn mid-year (higher interest/pressure costs), followed by wind-up before FY2028.

base.funding_source: Continued NZ Silveray Group loans/debt forgiveness, consistent with FY2020-FY2026 pattern
base.note: Revenue and burn shown for transparency on the cost of 'life support'; per the base-case methodology this burn is funded externally (shareholder loans/forgiveness) and is a wash against the tangible-equity valuation, not a further deduction from it.

bull.note: Only FY2027 transaction-cost burn is shown. Post-RTO cash flows belong to an undisclosed acquired business and are not modelled; bull IV is derived directly from shell-value precedent (see assumptions.bull), not from a discounted cash-flow sum.

bear.note: Wind-up assumed to occur during/immediately after FY2027 once shareholder support is withdrawn.

base.methodology: intrinsic_value = (FY2026 shareholders' equity + shell scarcity value) / shares outstanding = (206,390 + 500,000) / 3,664,253,194 = NZ$0.000193/share

bull.methodology: intrinsic_value = upper-precedent shell value / shares outstanding = 2,500,000 / 3,664,253,194 = NZ$0.000682/share. Even this generous, speculative RTO-completion scenario values the stock BELOW the current NZ$0.001 minimum-tick price.

bear.methodology: Direct insolvency/wind-up waterfall: realizable asset value < liabilities once related-party loans, other payables and liquidation costs are applied. Ordinary equity holders receive NZ$0.0000/share.

base.interim_distributions_note: No dividends, buybacks, or other cash distributions to shareholders have ever been made or are contemplated; the going-concern burn is funded by/for the company, not distributed, so interim cash flow to the equity holder is NIL under the base case.
base.exit_equity_value_note: Base-case exit value assumed structurally similar to today (tangible equity + shell scarcity value), consistent with the 'persists on life support' narrative - continued shareholder funding is assumed to keep book equity roughly stable, not to compound it.
base.net_debt_adjustment_note: Not applied separately - net debt is already embedded inside the FY2026 shareholders' equity figure used as the exit-value base (equity = assets minus all liabilities, including the related-party loan), so subtracting it again would double-count.
base.untradeable_note: This computed 15%-IRR entry price (NZ$0.0000958) is below the NZX minimum tick of NZ$0.001 and is therefore UNTRADEABLE - the market cannot quote or execute a price that low. The stock cannot currently be bought at a price consistent with a 15% IRR to any of the three scenarios; the only way to transact is at the NZ$0.001 floor, which every scenario values as substantially overpriced.

sensitivity.description: A standard WACC / terminal-growth grid is not meaningful here (no perpetuity cash-flow stream). Instead this matrix sensitizes the base-case intrinsic value to (rows) the degree of haircut applied to FY2026 tangible book equity - reflecting uncertainty over whether even currently-reported book equity is realizable, given related-party-dependent asset values - and (columns) the shell scarcity value assumption.
sensitivity.matrix_read_note: Row = equity haircut (0% = full FY2026 book equity of NZ$206,390 credited; 100% = book equity assumed entirely unrealizable, e.g. total insolvency of the vineyard/mask-plant carrying values). Column = shell scarcity value from NZ$0 (no RTO/promoter interest at all) to NZ$1.0M (near the top of historical precedent). Every single cell in this 5x5 grid is still far below the current NZ$0.001 price (which requires an implied equity value of ~NZ$3.66M just to be fair value at the floor tick).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear is weighted heaviest (55%) given the EXPLICIT auditor going-concern material uncertainty paragraph in the audited FY2026 financial statements, a working-capital deficit of NZ$1.3M, negative equity mid-year (H1-2026: -NZ$120,066) only restored by a one-off debt-forgiveness injection, and total dependence on a single related party's discretionary, NON-BINDING support letter that can be withdrawn at any time. Base (35%) reflects that NZSG has, to date, consistently chosen to keep funding the shell (forgave NZ$500,000 + waived NZ$281,170 interest in FY2026 alone, plus two further NZ$100,000 advances after year-end), so continued life-support is a real possibility, not just the bear case. Bull (10%) reflects that the Fast Track Group discussion is disclosed only as an MOU-stage, non-binding exploration among several alternatives being evaluated (including 'other M&A, equity placement, and water-infrastructure investment opportunities') - i.e., genuinely speculative with no certainty of terms or completion.

sanity_check.current_price_pb_note: At the NZ$0.001 minimum-tick price, market cap is ~NZ$3.664M against FY2026 shareholders' equity of NZ$206,390 - an implied Price/Book of ~17.7x. AFC has historically traded at high nominal P/B multiples ONLY because reported book equity has collapsed toward zero (equity fell from NZ$3.73M in FY2019 to NZ$0.21M in FY2026, a 94% decline) while the share price has been mechanically pinned at the NZX minimum tick throughout - i.e., the high P/B is an artifact of the price floor and a shrinking denominator, not a market judgment that the business is worth 17.7x its book value.
trip_reasons: Market price (NZ$0.001) is at the NZX minimum tick and has not moved in over 4 years (MonthlyPrices.txt shows NZ$0.001 in every month from late-2017 through Jul-2026, with brief NZ$0.002-0.004 prints only in 2016-2020) - it cannot mechanically fall further to reflect deteriorating fundamentals, so it structurally overstates intrinsic value in a way ordinary price-discovery would not permit for a liquid stock.
Implied P/B of ~17.7x at the price floor is far above what any of the three fundamentals-based scenarios (bear 0x, base ~3.4x, bull ~12.1x book) support.
All three scenario intrinsic values (NZ$0.0000, NZ$0.000193, NZ$0.000682) and the probability-weighted intrinsic value (NZ$0.000136) sit below the NZ$0.001 current price, most by 80-100%.

The computed 15%-IRR entry price (NZ$0.0000958) is itself below the exchange's minimum tradeable tick, meaning no price at which this stock could satisfy a normal return hurdle is actually executable on the NZX.
sanity_check.diagnosis: market price floor / option value, not fundamentals
sanity_check.fix_applied: asset-based scenario valuation instead of growth DCF

valuation_philosophy.no_positive_fcf_history: Reported FCF (which already deducts IFRS-16 lease principal) has been NEGATIVE in six of the seven fiscal years FY2020-FY2026, with the sole exception being FY2023 at +NZ$18,709 - an immaterial, working-capital-driven blip, not repeatable operating cash generation. FY2026 free cash flow was -NZ$631,437, the worst year on record, despite revenue also collapsing to a seven-year low of NZ$161,285. There is no genuine owner-FCF base to project growth from; any conventional DCF built off this series would either extrapolate an unrepeatable one-off (FY2023) or compound a structural cash-burn machine into a nonsensical negative-infinity or wildly-negative valuation. That is why this model abandons the FCF-projection framework entirely in favor of an asset/scenario approach.
valuation_philosophy.going_concern: The FY2026 audited financial statements (Grant Thornton, newly appointed after William Buck's July 2025 resignation) contain an explicit material uncertainty paragraph related to going concern. The Group has a working-capital deficit of NZ$1.3M, cash of only NZ$39,437 (of which NZ$37,345 is restricted as a bank guarantee, leaving effectively NIL free cash), and continues to operate only because its controlling shareholder, NZ Silveray Group Limited, has repeatedly chosen to forgive debt (NZ$500,000 in FY2026) and waive interest (NZ$281,170 in FY2026) and inject fresh advances (a further NZ$200,000 post-year-end). That support is governed only by a non-binding letter and can be withdrawn at NZSG's sole discretion at any time.
valuation_philosophy.value_rests_on_option_and_scarcity: To the extent this equity is worth anything above zero, that value rests almost entirely on (a) a small listed-shell scarcity premium to RTO promoters seeking a quick route to an NZX listing, and (b) speculative, unpriced optionality on the disclosed-but-unconfirmed Fast Track Group reverse-takeover MOU (or an alternative M&A/RTO transaction) actually completing on terms that leave existing holders with meaningful retained value after dilution. Neither is a cash-flow claim on AFC's actual wine/cosmetics operations, which are sub-scale (51%-owned, minority economics to AFC even before further dilution), collapsing in revenue, and have never generated a repeatable operating profit.
valuation_philosophy.weighted_iv_far_below_price_floor: The probability-weighted intrinsic value across all three scenarios (NZ$0.000136/share) sits roughly 86% below the current NZ$0.001 minimum-tick price, and even the single most optimistic scenario modelled (a completed RTO valuing the shell at the top of historical NZX shell-value precedent, NZ$0.000682/share) remains roughly 32% below the current price.
valuation_philosophy.uninvestable_conclusion: AFC.NZ is effectively uninvestable on a fundamentals basis at any currently tradeable price. The NZ$0.001 minimum tick is a structural floor of the NZX quotation system, not a market-clearing valuation of the underlying business - the stock has been unable to price below this floor for over four years even as reported book equity fell 94% over the same period. Any perceived 'value' in owning AFC shares today is a leveraged, binary bet on an unconfirmed reverse-takeover transaction completing on favorable terms, not a claim on any existing or foreseeable cash-generating business.
